newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-BONDS TO FAIL AT 113-03 UPSIDE BARRIER.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-BONDS TO FAIL AT 113-03 UPSIDE BARRIER.

text.p: September T-bond futures are not expected to push through a barrier at 113-03 on Tuesday and the bias will remain to the downside, technical analysts said.
David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London said over the past week T-bonds had been behaving differently to European bonds and would continue to do so.
"The pressure still remains to the downside," he said. "Ideally I would look for the 113-03, 113-12 area to cap the market and provoke a move back down to test the recent low at 112-08."
The 112-08 level was also marked by a long term support trendline, he said.
At 1015 GMT, September T-bond futures were at 112-29, up 5/32 in automated trade.
If 112-08 broke, Sneddon said T-bonds would slip to the 111-18, 111-14 zone.
"From there we should see a decent bounce up again," he said.
Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International in London also noted key support at 112-08.

"If it holds that level, the market is likely to rebound, but any bounce should be only a retracement," she said. "The market is still in a bear trend, and any short-term rebound is likely to be limited."
To the upside Liu put first resistance at 113-10, then 113-18.

Analysts said the market would also be influenced by fundamentals with various U.S. data due later in the session including the July Atlanta Fed Index at 1300 GMT and second quarter productivity and unit labour costs and the July Richmond Fed survey at 1400 GMT.
At the short end December Eurodollars were at 94.010, up 0.010 on the day.
